disclaimer.title: This app is not medical advice
disclaimer.intro: Qbit Nutrition is a tool for keeping a personal food log. It is not a medical device and does not diagnose, treat, or prevent any condition.

estimates.body: Calories and nutrients calculated from a photo are approximations produced with the help of an AI model you chose. They can be wrong, sometimes by a lot. Do not rely on them for medical decisions, such as insulin dosing or managing an allergy.

targets.body: Suggested calorie and nutrient targets come from standard formulas for healthy adults. They do not take your medical history into account.

professional.body: Consult a doctor or a registered dietitian before changing your diet, especially if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, under 18, have a medical condition, or have or have had an eating disorder.

allergens.body: Never use it to decide whether a food is safe for you.

disclaimer.closing: If tracking food causes you distress, stop using the app and seek support from a health professional.

update.title: The health notice changed
update.intro: The text of the health notice was updated. Please read it again before you continue. Your data has not been touched.
update.declinedTitle: The app needs this notice to be accepted
update.declinedBody: Your data is still on this phone and has not been changed. You can read the notice again, or close the app.
update.failed: The acceptance could not be saved. Try again.

summary.body: Your data stays on your device. We, the maintainers, do not collect, receive, or store any of it.

stores.lead: What the app stores on your device.
stores.body: Your profile (if you fill it in), goals, meals, nutrient values, body measurements, meal photos (if you keep them), and your AI provider settings. API keys are stored in your device's secure storage.

leaves.lead: What leaves your device, and only when you trigger it.

photo.data: The photo (reduced in size, without location metadata), your optional hint, your language

suggest.data: Remaining calories and nutrients for the day, your goal, your language

barcode.data: The barcode number, and the app name, version and project address in the request header

leaves.note: Your AI provider processes what you send under its own terms and privacy policy, which you accepted when you created your account with it. Some providers use content sent on free plans to improve their products. Check your provider's terms. If you use a model running on your own computer, nothing is sent to a third party. Like any web service, the AI provider and Open Food Facts also see your network address when they receive a request.

never.body: No accounts, no analytics, no advertising, no crash reports, no tracking, no selling or sharing of data.

health.body: If you turn on Health Connect, the app writes each saved meal to it as a nutrition record (time, meal type, calories, nutrients and the meal's name) and reads your weight from it, on your device, with the permissions you grant. The two permissions are separate and you can decline either. Other apps that you allow in Health Connect can read what this app wrote. You can turn it off in the app and revoke the permissions in system settings at any time. Deleting all data in the app offers to remove the records it wrote.

control.body: You can export all your data, delete it all from Settings → Data, or uninstall the app, which removes everything it stored. Records already written to Health Connect belong to Health Connect: remove them with the option in Delete all data, or in Health Connect itself.

children.body: The app is intended for adults.

changes.body: Changes to this policy are published in the project repository with the release that introduces them.

about.title: About
about.privacy: Your data stays on this phone. Only what you choose to send leaves it: a meal photo, or the numbers behind a food suggestion, to the AI provider you set up; a barcode number to Open Food Facts; and the files you export. There is no account and no analytics.

sources.title: Data sources
sources.usda: Food composition data: U.S. Department of Agriculture, Agricultural Research Service. FoodData Central.
sources.off: Product data: Open Food Facts, made available under the Open Database License (ODbL), with individual contents under the Database Contents License. Products are looked up one barcode at a time and saved on this phone; the database is not included in the app.
sources.offLink: Open Food Facts license and terms
sources.usdaNote: The nutrient values in the bundled food list come from this source: Foundation Foods, SR Legacy and Survey Foods (FNDDS 2021-2023), all in the public domain (CC0 1.0). A food published by more than one of them appears once. Spanish names and search synonyms were written for this app and contain no nutrient values.
sources.recipesNote: Some regional dishes (milanesa, empanadas, locro, mate and others) are not laboratory data: they are calculated by the authors of this app from a documented recipe and the values of its ingredients in the list above, using cooking yields and vitamin retention factors published by the U.S. Department of Agriculture. They are marked "Calculated from a recipe" and open to show their ingredients. Real dishes vary, so read them as a typical estimate. The method is described in the source code of the app.
sources.importedNote: Food tables you import yourself (for example a national table you downloaded from its publisher) come from that publisher and keep that publisher’s license, which applies to your use. They are read on this phone, stay on it, and are not part of this app or its source code. Each such food shows the name of the table you gave it.
sources.offNote: Product images from Open Food Facts are not used.

health.title: Integrations
health.intro: Health Connect is the Android place where health apps share data on your phone. It stays off unless you turn it on here.

rationale.title: What Qbit Nutrition uses Health Connect for
rationale.intro: These are the two kinds of data, and why each one is used. Nothing else is read or written.

nutrition.title: Nutrition
nutrition.body: Each meal you save becomes a nutrition record: when you ate, the meal type, calories, protein, carbohydrates, fat, and the fiber, sugars, sodium and vitamins and minerals this app tracks. This lets your other health apps show what you ate. Editing or deleting a meal here updates or removes its record.

weight.title: Weight
weight.body: Weight entries from the last 30 days are copied into this app so they appear in your weight chart. They are marked as coming from Health Connect. Nothing about weight is written back.

rationale.separate: You can allow one of the two and decline the other. The other still works.
rationale.local: Health Connect keeps its data on this phone. Photos, AI provider details and keys are never shared with it.
rationale.revoke: You can turn this off here, or take access away in Health Connect, at any time.

add.formats: Reads spreadsheets (.xlsx, .xls) and text files (.csv). A PDF or a web page cannot be read: look for the spreadsheet version.

map.title: Match the columns
map.intro: Check what was found in the file. Change anything that is wrong; nothing is saved yet.
map.headerRowHint: The row with the column names. Foods start below it.
map.name: Food name
map.unitRefused: This unit can’t be converted for this nutrient.
map.basisAssumed: The file does not say, so 100 g is assumed. Change it if the table says otherwise.
map.basisMl: Per 100 ml is kept as written and flagged. The app counts amounts in grams, so 1 ml counts as 1 g.
map.basisKg: Per 1 kg is divided by 10 to give per 100 g.
map.basisOther2: Per portion, per serving or per 100 kcal cannot become per 100 g without inventing a weight. This table cannot be imported.
map.decimalFound: Detected from the numbers in the file.
map.nutrientsHint: Only what the app tracks. Columns you leave out are not imported.
map.rulesExact: Numbers are kept exactly as written. The only change is the unit conversion below (and dividing by 10 for a per 1 kg table). Nothing is estimated, rounded or filled in.
map.rulesUnknown: These mean “no value” and are stored as unknown, never as zero: {{markers}}. So do empty cells, “less than” values and text that is not a number.
map.rulesUnits: Units: kJ ÷ 4.184 = kcal. g, mg and µg convert exactly. Vitamin D in IU: 40 IU = 1 µg. Vitamin A and other vitamins in IU are refused, because the factor depends on the compound.

problem.no_foods: No row has a name and a value.
